newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish ABB unit's 1996 net soars to PLN 115 mln.
newsitem.headline: Polish ABB unit's 1996 net soars to PLN 115 mln.

text.p: Asea Brown Boveri's Polish unit increased its net profit to 115 million zlotys last year from 62 million zlotys in 1995 thanks to cost cutting, the unit's head said on Thursday.

"The net profit rise by 85 percent...was possible thanks to a substantial reduction of own costs," Miroslaw Gryszka told a news conference. He added the cost cuts were achieved mainly through modernisation.
Gryszka said the unit's revenues rose to 1.3 billion zlotys last year from 1.01 billion zlotys in 1995. The unit's exports fell by $9 million to $87 million.
The unit, which now controls 13 Polish firms employing 6,200 workers, also plans new acquisitions, Gryszka said.
"ABB plans to further develop in Poland...We envisage purchases of companies undergoing privatisation or those already privatised," he said.
ABB, eleventh largest foreign investor in Poland, has brought more than $200 million to the east European country since 1990. It invested $36 million last year.
The firm has recently bought a 60 percent stake of electric power measurement devices maker Elbud, based in the northen city of Elblag, from the National Investment Funds (NFI).
The ABB unit is also bidding for the ZWAR factory, producting the same equimpent in Warsaw.
